title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Tuesday morning, Nov 17
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 7:30 AM ET Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). Two new Right-wing stories lead this morning. Protesters briefly drove former Border Patrol commander Greg Bovino off a Rutgers stage Monday night, and 'the left shut down free speech' clips sent the Bovino query from a prior daily average of about 7 posts to 10,956 in 24 hours, 10,251 of them overnight. Elon Musk ('She's just an actor') and Spencer Pratt revived the 2017 claim that Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez 'answered a casting call,' sending that query to 14,315 posts (108× its prior average). The recruitment is real and public; the 'actor' part is a smear Snopes examined years ago. 'Texas Democrats are coming for your guns' held at 3,729 posts (3.62×). Van Hollen vs. Schumer is still the largest conversation (20,004 posts) but cooling as Senate Democrats meet today and show little appetite to move up the Dec. 1 vote. On the left, the anti-Jeffries petition has passed a million signatures, and Jeffries says he will call his own recorded vote at Wednesday's caucus meeting. A disinformation note: today's routine 2:20 PM ET Emergency Alert System test spawned a '90-day blackout' hoax (8,570 posts on a related query). PolitiFact rates it False. Every count, quote, and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this morning or carried over from last evening and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

trends.detail: U.S. trends were pulled at about 7:09 AM ET with x.get_trends_by_woeid (WOEID 23424977, max 50; 48 returned). Sports (Chargers, Ravens, Lamar, Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers), K-pop and Thai fan events, and international news (Philippines, Crimea, Kerch, ASEAN, APEC) dominated. 'FEMA' and 'Emergency Alert System' reflect today's nationwide EAS test, which is covered in the FAA card's blackout-hoax section, but that query is not scored. 'Dirty Bomb' and 'Air Force One' did not match any scored query, and we did not research them further. None of the eighteen scored narratives appeared on the U.S. trends list, so no card received the trend bonus. We requested tweet_count, but the trend objects did not include it, so trend volumes are unavailable and we did not estimate them.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. Several stories this morning are worked by both sides. The Right amplifies the speaker-race fights and Sen. John Fetterman's 'red line' as a 'Democratic civil war,' while the 'casting call' attack on Ocasio-Cortez lands just as NYC-DSA talks her up for 2028. The Nov. 17 blackout hoax is not clearly partisan (crypto and doomsday accounts drove much of it), so it sits inside the FAA card rather than getting its own score. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026, 7:30 AM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 7:09 AM ET. Last evening's snapshot (Nov 16, 5:25 PM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Sixteen of its seventeen narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps last evening's by 10 hours (7 AM to 5 PM ET Monday), so we also report each query's 5 PM–7 AM ET overnight count against the same hours a night earlier. One narrative was dropped because it faded: Melat Kiros and the 'earn my vote' bloc (465 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.84× its prior daily average, down from 1,785 last evening); her demands still appear in the Jeffries cards. Two were added with new queries: the Bovino event at Rutgers and the AOC 'casting call' claim. Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: Fetterman's threat to leave the party (3,302 posts, 0.84×), which is folded into the Van Hollen card; a narrower Jeffries + Iran + AIPAC query (34 posts across the Nov. 16 and Nov. 17 UTC bars); and a broader filibuster query (2,812 posts across the same bars). An Emergency Alert System + blackout/attack query (8,570 posts in 24 hours, 16.07×) is reported inside the FAA card and not scored, because much of its volume is official test notices.

For each narrative we ran English-language X searches with x.get_posts_counts_recent: hourly granularity for a window from 7:00 AM ET Monday, Nov 16, through 7:00 AM ET Tuesday, Nov 17 (exactly 24 hours), and daily granularity for a 167-hour 'seven-day' window from 8:00 AM ET Tuesday, Nov 10 (the earliest whole-hour start the recent-count API allowed at pull time) to the same end point. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved in this morning's searches and cite on the card. Official government pages, bill text, advocacy groups, research groups, pollsters, bill trackers, blogs, X News summaries, and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets. Sources carried over from last evening without being re-retrieved are not counted, which is why some cards' outlet counts changed. We noted whether each topic appeared on the U.S. trends list at about 7:09 AM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list this morning. The Bovino, AOC, 'Make America Nice Again' and Buttigieg queries had near-zero baselines, so their acceleration indices max out; read the post counts alongside the scores.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The Jeffries/AIPAC, Pressley, Leonard and DSA queries share many speaker-race posts. The Leonard query includes the bare name 'Leonard,' the AOC query includes the bare word 'cast,' and the rigged-midterms query also catches posts mocking fraud claims. Replies are included, and automated @grok replies make up a visible share of several queries. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This morning we pulled fresh samples for Bovino, the AOC 'casting call,' Texas gun bills, Van Hollen, and the blackout hoax. Other cards carry last evening's sentiment and say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatLead: A fact-check is not a volume score.
disinfo.caveatBody: New this morning: there is no Nov. 17 blackout. Today's 2:20 PM ET nationwide Emergency Alert System test is a routine check required at least every three years, on TV and radio only. PolitiFact rates the '90-day blackout' claim False and found a TikTok clip of President Trump 'announcing' it was manipulated from a Nov. 9 briefing. Snopes and France 24 trace the rumor to last week's outages, Simpsons references, and crypto accounts urging people to pull their savings. 'AOC is an actor who answered a casting call' twists a real, public fact: Justice Democrats recruited her after her brother nominated her, which Snopes found routine for PACs; voters then elected her. 'Gov. Sherrill tried to stop Bovino from speaking' is misleading: she criticized the invitation, promised to protect the event, and it went ahead. The anti-Jeffries petition really has passed a million signatures, but Change.org signatures are not verified voters. Carried over: Monday's bank outages were not shown to be a cyberattack; 'Texas Democrats banned guns for under-21s' is false (HB 606 is only prefiled); 'Jeffries took $1.5 million from AIPAC' conflates different money streams; Lead Stories found no '30,000-case' Texas voter fraud probe; the reparations bill (SB 376) does not pay reparations and is only prefiled; 'Slotkin is a CIA asset' remains unsupported; and the 'Seditious Six' face no DOJ case after a grand jury declined to indict.

Mikie Sherrill's statement an 'attack on free speech.' A minority of replies argued that criticizing a speaker is not censorship. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this morning, and the fastest riser in the set. The query matched 10,956 posts in the last 24 hours, against a prior daily average of just 7.2. Almost all of it came after the event: 705 posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Monday, then 10,251 from 5 PM to 7 AM ET, peaking at 2,326 posts at 7 PM ET Monday. Former Border Patrol commander Greg Bovino spoke Monday night at a Rutgers Republicans event in New Brunswick. NJ.com reported that protesters' screams drowned him out and police ushered him away, then brought him back about 10 minutes later, when he spoke to about 50 people while about 100 chanted outside. The Philadelphia Inquirer put the crowd outside at more than 200, and organizers told News 12 about 300. Earlier Monday, Gov. Mikie Sherrill said Bovino 'chose cruelty over humanity,' but also said the state would work with Rutgers to protect public safety and constitutional rights, and the event went ahead. Bovino was removed from command in January after federal agents shot and killed Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis, and he retired in March. On stage he called the governor 'Sugar Pop' Sherrill. The top post, from @RyanAFournier ('You have NO RIGHT to shut down free speech'), drew 2,087 likes and 40,280 views.
talkingPoints: The left can't handle free speech — they shouted down a Border Patrol hero.
You have every right to protest. You have no right to shut down a speaker.
A Democratic governor attacked students for inviting a conservative.
He came back and finished the speech. They lost.
This is what the new Democratic majority looks like on campus.
narratives.amplifiers: @RyanAFournier (2,087 likes, 613 reposts, 40,280 views); @Ravious101 (243 likes, 7,475 views); @EricLDaugh (footage, per quoting posts); @iDenville; @defnoodlesreal; @MDBayNews and @NathanielSami on Sherrill's statement.
narratives.whyItWorks: Campus shout-downs are a reliable Right-wing story because the video does the work: a calm speaker, a screaming crowd, police in between. It also pins the disruption on the new Democratic governor and recasts an immigration fight as a free-speech fight, where the Right is more comfortable.
narratives.audience: Conservatives, free-speech and anti-'woke campus' voters, parents of college students, and immigration hawks.
narratives.counter: Separate the two things. The governor criticized the invitation and promised to protect the event, and it went ahead. Shouting down a speaker is a bad look and a gift to him; say so. Then bring it back to the record people were protesting: two Americans killed in Minneapolis on his watch.

factChecks.claim: Gov. Mikie Sherrill tried to stop Greg Bovino from speaking at Rutgers.
factChecks.detail: Sherrill condemned the Rutgers Republicans' invitation and urged students to challenge Bovino, but said the state would work with Rutgers to protect public safety and constitutional rights. Rutgers said the club was permitted to host him, and the event went ahead after a roughly 10-minute interruption. This is TDDR's read of NJ.com and CBS New York reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from the last 24 hours, nearly every top match repeated the 'casting call' framing — 'AOC is an actor,' 'Manchurian Candidate,' 'she still reads the script' — often as replies under @spencerpratt or @elonmusk. A few replies (and automated @grok answers) explained that Justice Democrats and Brand New Congress recruited candidates through public nominations. The query includes the bare word 'cast,' which can catch unrelated posts, but the sample was dominated by this narrative. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this morning. The query matched 14,315 posts in the last 24 hours, 108 times its prior daily average of 132. From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Monday it matched 10,610 posts, and 3,705 more overnight. Hourly volume peaked at 1,605 posts at 9 AM ET Monday. Two posts drove it. Late Sunday, @elonmusk replied 'She's just an actor. Her words are written by others' (61,192 likes, 1,488,094 views when we pulled it) and, early Monday, 'She does have some skills as an actor' (11,872 likes, 304,356 views). At 6:48 AM ET Monday, @spencerpratt posted that 'the Agent of Communism AOC answered a casting call from the "Justice Democrats"' and was 'groomed by a socialist PAC' into 'a legit Manchurian Candidate' (27,293 likes, 8,846 reposts, 189,530 views). The core facts are old and public: in 2016–17, Justice Democrats and Brand New Congress solicited nominations for candidates, Ocasio-Cortez's brother nominated her while she worked at a restaurant, and the groups recruited her. Snopes examined the 'actress' version in 2019 and found the recruitment real but routine for PACs; Ocasio-Cortez then won a contested 2018 primary and has been re-elected by voters since. The story resurfaces as NYC-DSA urges her to run for president in 2028 and Punchbowl News reports senators speculating about a Schumer primary.
talkingPoints: AOC answered a casting call — she's an actor playing a congresswoman.
A socialist PAC picked her out of 10,000 applicants and wrote her script.
Her words are written by others.
Bartender to Manchurian Candidate.
If she's a puppet, who are the puppet masters?
narratives.amplifiers: @elonmusk ('She's just an actor,' 61,192 likes, 1.49M views; 'some skills as an actor,' 11,872 likes, 304,356 views); @spencerpratt (27,293 likes, 8,846 reposts, 189,530 views); @MagaQueen47; @pdxmoderate; and many reply-chain accounts. X News ran a summary: 'Old Claims Resurface That AOC Answered Justice Democrats Casting Call.'
narratives.whyItWorks: It takes a true, slightly unusual fact — a PAC recruited her through public nominations — and turns it into a story about puppets and scripts. That lets critics dismiss everything she says without engaging it, and it lands just as the left talks her up for 2028 or a Senate run.
narratives.audience: Conservatives and MAGA-aligned users, Musk's audience, and voters who distrust 'manufactured' politicians on any side.
narratives.counter: Don't deny the recruitment; own it. Groups on both sides recruit candidates, and voters in the Bronx and Queens chose her in a primary nobody expected her to win, then re-elected her. Ask why picking a bartender over a donor's favorite is the scandal.

factChecks.claim: AOC is an actress who was cast to play a congresswoman.
factChecks.detail: Snopes found that Justice Democrats did recruit Ocasio-Cortez after her brother nominated her, but that recruiting candidates is common for PACs and the group discussed it openly. The video that popularized the 'actress' claim was, by its creator's own account, 'illustrative.' She was elected by voters in a 2018 primary and general election.

From 5 PM ET Monday to 7 AM ET Tuesday the query matched 1,310 posts, versus 1,461 in the same hours a night earlier. USA Today and KRLD/Audacy coverage confirms roughly 20 bills were filed. All are prefiled for a session that opens Jan. 12, 2027. Near-identical copies of that list and a '🚨 almost two dozen anti-gun bills' template made up most of the top matches. The bills are real. Snopes counted 25 firearm-related bills prefiled for 2027, filed by 11 Democrats and three Republicans. HB 606 (Rep. Suleman Lalani, D) would bar anyone under 21 from buying or possessing any firearm, and SB 80 (Sen. Judith Zaffirini, D) would restrict 'assault weapons.' Both texts take effect Sept. 1, 2027, only if passed, and the session does not open until Jan. 12, 2027. No bill has had a hearing. This morning's card (7:30 AM ET): 1,831 posts in the last 24 hours, 1.50 times its prior daily average. Volume rose from single digits Sunday morning to 259 posts at 6 PM ET and stayed above 100 an hour until 11 PM ET. The biggest post was @EricLDaugh's 'Almost TWO DOZEN anti-firearm bills have been filed in the Texas Legislature as Democrats sweep the statewide elections' (5,650 likes, 2,000 reposts, 247,869 views), copied by many accounts. The core fact is accurate. Snopes found 25 firearm-related bills prefiled for the 2027 session. Their authors include 11 Democrats and 3 Republicans, and some bills (on sex offenders or vehicle burglary) are not gun control in the usual sense. The Texan and the NRA's lobbying arm list the main ones: HB 606, which would bar people under 21 from buying or possessing firearms; HB 173 and similar bills limiting semiautomatic-rifle transfers to people under 21; HB 613 on private-sale background checks; HB 218, red-flag orders; and SB 80, an assault-weapons ban. Prefiling opened Nov. 9, the session starts Jan. 12, 2027, and Republicans still control the Texas Senate.
talkingPoints: The first thing Democrats did with power in Texas was come for your guns.
No grandfather clause: under-21s would lose guns they already own.
Six days after they flipped the Texas House, Democrats came for the guns.
They ran on affordability and filed two dozen gun bills.
Red flag orders and gun registries are how disarmament starts.
If it can happen in Texas, it can happen anywhere.
narratives.amplifiers: Named accounts in posts we opened this evening: @bennyjohnson (5,337 likes, 1,926 reposts, 140,381 views); @stevegrubershow ('23 gun bills on day one,' 29 likes, 1,003 views); @UnmaskTheSys (16 likes, 1,225 views); @mcafeenew (15 likes, 1,294 views); @ConstitustionX (625 views); @YoungRightUS; and copy-paste accounts. narratives.whyItWorks: Gun rights are an identity issue in Texas, and a list of bill numbers looks like proof of a plan. It also turns the Democrats' surprise statewide wins into a warning for every other red state.
narratives.audience: Texas gun owners, Second Amendment groups, rural and suburban conservatives, and gun-owning swing voters who backed Democrats on affordability.
narratives.counter: Be precise: about 25 bills were prefiled, including some by Republicans, and none has had a hearing. Republicans control the Texas Senate. Many of the bills are age limits, background checks, or child-access penalties that poll well even among gun owners. Don't defend an 'assault weapons ban' that has no path; talk about what voters actually asked for.

narratives.title: FAA ground stop, day 5 — and the 'Nov. 17 blackout' hoax rides today's emergency alert test
narratives.query: (FAA OR "ground stop" OR "air traffic" OR groundstop) (Buttigieg OR "Mayor Pete" OR cyberattack OR "cyber attack" OR hacked OR sabotage) lang:en
narratives.sentimentNote: We did not pull a fresh sample of the FAA query this evening. A separate sample of bank-outage posts since 1 PM ET Monday mixed straight news ('AP reports … no indication that a cyber-attack') with speculation ('Biggest Cyber attack,' 'Has a massive cyber attack on the US banking system … begun?'). Automated @grok replies mostly said Chase confirmed a technical issue. Morning note on the FAA query:  This morning's sentiment label is carried over from last evening's sample; we did not pull a fresh sample for this card.
narratives.summary: Morning update (Nov 17): 8,584 posts in the last 24 hours, 1.05 times the prior daily average (last evening: 9,809 and 1.32×). From 5 PM ET Monday to 7 AM ET Tuesday the query matched 3,324 posts, versus 4,544 in the same hours a night earlier. New this morning: today's routine nationwide Emergency Alert System test (2:20 PM ET, TV and radio only, not phones) became a '90-day blackout' rumor. A separate EAS + blackout/attack query matched 8,570 posts in the last 24 hours (16.07× its prior daily average), 6,902 of them since 5 PM ET Monday. Much of that volume is official notices from emergency-management offices, so we report it here and do not score it. PolitiFact rated the blackout claim False and found that a TikTok clip of President Trump 'announcing' a 90-day blackout was manipulated from a Nov. 9 briefing. Snopes and France 24 say the rumor fed on last week's ground stop, the Microsoft and bank outages, Simpsons references, and crypto accounts urging people to pull their savings. U.S. trends at about 7:09 AM ET included 'FEMA' and 'Emergency Alert System.' On the ground stop itself, the FAA says there is no indication of a cyberattack, and Fortune reports the FBI is assisting the investigation. Last evening's card: Evening update: 9,809 posts in the last 24 hours, 1.32 times the prior daily average (this morning: 9,982 and 1.54×). From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Monday the query matched 5,265 posts, versus 5,434 in the same hours Sunday. Trump said Monday he bears no responsibility for Friday's ground stop and blamed the Biden administration for aging equipment (USA Today; The Washington Post covered his first comments Sunday). Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy again pointed to a newly installed router during the copper-to-fiber upgrade. A new outage then revived the 'we're under cyberattack' frame. On Monday afternoon, customers at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and Zelle reported problems. Posts chained the FAA stop, last week's Microsoft outage and the banks together ('NOW DO YOU THINK WE'RE UNDER CYBER ATTACK?'). A separate bank-outage + cyberattack query matched 767 posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET (versus 159 in the same hours Sunday), climbing from 66 posts at 1 PM ET to 242 at 3 PM. JPMorgan Chase said the cause was 'a software bug in on-premise hardware systems — there is no evidence this is cyber-related' (AP, CNBC, BBC, WIRED), and a Justice Department official told MS NOW there was 'no evidence of any attack' and no indication of a link to Friday's outages. This morning's card (7:30 AM ET): Still large but cooling: 9,982 posts in the last 24 hours, down from 11,592 in last night's window, at 1.54 times its prior daily average. Its score fell from 73 to 66. Volume ran about 450 to 730 posts an hour through Sunday daytime and fell below 200 an hour overnight. The official account hasn't changed. The FAA's Q&A says 'we have no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor,' and that the data flood traced to a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris had installed a new router, and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas. USA Today reports both facilities are under scrutiny. ABC News reports Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the routers' ability to broadcast data has been turned off while investigators work. The Transportation Department says Duffy used the Sunday shows to push to finish air-traffic-control modernization. AP reports the administration is asking for billions to overhaul the FAA, and Democrats are questioning how earlier money was spent. Posts say Trump blamed the Biden administration on Sunday; we did not confirm the exact quote.
talkingPoints: FAA, Microsoft, now the banks — how many 'glitches' before they admit it's an attack?
It was a botched contractor upgrade on a system Buttigieg left to rot.
Remember Christmas Eve 2024? Nobody blamed Mayor Pete then.
Give Duffy the money and finish air traffic control modernization.
They say 'no cyberattack' every time — the investigation isn't finished.
narratives.amplifiers: Named voices in coverage and posts we opened: the FAA's Q&A; Secretary Duffy on the Sunday shows, per the Transportation Department and ABC News; @ToscaAusten's 'Mayor Pete' post (174 likes, 165 reposts, 4,625 views); @TaxmanTm ('A botched routine upgrade'); and @shadowgrid7. Automated @grok replies remain a visible share of matches.
narratives.whyItWorks: A miserable travel weekend needs a villain, and the official explanation hands each side one: the Right gets a contractor, a decades-old system, and a funding ask, plus the 'Mayor Pete did it too' callback; Democrats get a resignation demand and an oversight hook.
narratives.audience: Pro-administration posters defending Duffy, conservative media audiences, travelers still caught in the recovery, and Democrats preparing January oversight.

X News clustered 'Democrats Consider Tax Increases for 2027 Spending Plans' Monday afternoon. The new Congress is not seated until January, and coverage notes a Trump veto could block enactment. This morning's card (7:30 AM ET): Still rising fast, though off last night's peak: 2,638 posts in the last 24 hours, 3.57 times its prior daily average (last night's window: 3,310). Volume peaked between 9 and 10 AM ET Sunday (228 and 240 posts an hour), held above 100 an hour through 9 PM ET, and dropped below 30 an hour overnight. X News updated its cluster again overnight. The underlying Wall Street Journal report, as quoted by Political Wire, says Democrats have 'a broad consensus to reverse President Trump's tariffs' and the Medicaid, food-stamp, and health-subsidy cuts. It says 'party lawmakers are weighing when to attach tax increases.' Options discussed include a 39.6 percent top rate and higher corporate and capital-gains taxes. talkingPoints: Democrats won on affordability, and their first idea is raising your taxes.
39.6% is back on the table before they're even sworn in.
A $5 trillion wish list means tax hikes for everyone, not just billionaires.
Reversing Trump's tariffs and tax cuts is a tax increase by another name.
narratives.amplifiers: Named accounts in posts we opened: @GuntherEagleman (279 likes, 111 reposts, 14,435 views) and copy-paste versions from @real_jfkjr01 and @theletter17_; @Cmfover84 ('39.6% is back on the table,' 14 likes, 635 views); @Momo_Douk45 (423 views); and @PatriotAndPoise. X News kept its cluster updated overnight.
narratives.whyItWorks: Affordability won Democrats the midterms, so 'they'll raise your taxes' attacks the brand at its strongest point. It's also partly true — Democrats are debating tax increases — which makes the exaggeration ('on Americans') harder to rebut in one line.
narratives.audience: Conservative and libertarian voters, small-business owners, and swing voters who backed Democrats on costs. Also likely to resonate with moderate Democrats wary of the party's left.
narratives.counter: Say who pays. The proposals on the table target incomes over roughly $1 million and corporations, and Trump can veto all of it until 2029. Put the trade on the table plainly: restoring Medicaid, SNAP, and ACA subsidies for working families, paid for by the top bracket. Don't deny that a debate over tax increases is happening — it is.

factChecks.claim: Democrats are planning 'major tax hikes on Americans' for 2027.
factChecks.detail: The Wall Street Journal report, as quoted by Political Wire, says Democrats are 'weighing when to attach tax increases' to bills reversing Medicaid, SNAP, and health-subsidy cuts — a debate, not a passed plan. The Tax Foundation says the proposals on the table target high-income individuals and corporations and that any tax increase is 'limited by President Trump’s veto.' Viral posts dropped both caveats. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

Vox describes the plan she has pitched for a Democratic majority in three parts: housing and health-care bills, accountability in 'signature cases' of alleged misuse of taxpayer money and power, and reforms so no future president can exploit the same weaknesses. talkingPoints: Slotkin is ex-CIA, and there's no such thing as ex-CIA.
'Reimagine the systems' means tear up the Constitution.
This is the color-revolution playbook from Eastern Europe, now on American soil.
She went to Hungary and Poland to learn how to take down a government.
narratives.amplifiers: Named accounts in posts we opened: @stevegrubershow (1,403 likes, 723 reposts, 30,945 views); @Keltic_Spirit, 'Elissa Slotkin is a CIA asset' (272 likes, 161 reposts, 3,326 views); @BrettDoyleMCS ('went to Hungary on an exercise of Color Revolution'); and pro-Slotkin template accounts such as @Alexwestlivee.
narratives.whyItWorks: It fuses a true biographical fact (she worked at the CIA) with a vague quote ('build something new') and an existing Right-wing frame ('color revolution'). Listeners can fill a vague quote with their worst fears, and the biography makes the conspiracy feel like evidence.
narratives.audience: MAGA-aligned and conspiracy-curious audiences, Trump supporters primed by the 'Seditious Six' posts, and some anti-establishment voters on the left who distrust the intelligence agencies.
narratives.counter: Play the tape; don't paraphrase it. The Carnegie event was about broad coalitions, anti-corruption cases, and free elections, the same tools the Right praised when they were used against governments it opposed. Don't defend vague language, either. Ask Slotkin to name the 'systems' she means.

factChecks.claim: Slotkin's call to 'reimagine and build something new' after Trump is a CIA-run 'color revolution' plan to overthrow the government.
factChecks.detail: The remarks appear to come from a public Carnegie Endowment event billed as lessons from Hungary and Poland on defending democracy. Her office's summary describes building coalitions, exposing corruption, and protecting free elections. Posts making the 'CIA asset' claim offered no evidence beyond her past CIA employment. We found no fact-check outlet rating the claim; this is TDDR's read of the event record and the coverage we retrieved.
